established_findings.statement: Large language models can synthesize network-configuration templates and translate high-level intents into low-level configurations with promising accuracy in controlled/emulated tasks.
limitations: Evaluations are primarily on controlled tasks, limited topologies, or exercise-focused profiles rather than heterogeneous production networks
Human-provided critical information or few-shot examples often remained part of the workflow

established_findings.statement: When asked to repair misconfigured networks, LLMs can produce fixes but frequently introduce regressions and their performance degrades with scale or complexity unless integrated into verifier-guided workflows.
limitations: Cornetto and WirelessOptBench use synthesized or bench-simulated scenarios; exact behavior in diverse production settings is not established
Model set and exact prompting choices materially affect outcomes

established_findings.statement: Architectures that combine LLM generation with deterministic validators, sandboxed/simulated execution, RAG, and iterative repair/self-correction materially improve operational reliability compared to generator-only pipelines.
limitations: Improvements are shown in experimental/sandboxed settings; integration cost, latency, and operator workflow implications vary by deployment
Degree of improvement depends on specificity and strength of the validator/simulator used

established_findings.statement: Current benchmarks and evaluation practices for LLM-driven NetOps risk weak construct validity unless they explicitly tie tasks to operational metrics (e.g., reachability, policy compliance, unsafe-apply rate) and execution-time evidence checks.
limitations: Construct-validity critique is general; concrete alternative metrics and standardized protocols remain underdeveloped
Some recent benchmarks (e.g., Cornetto, WirelessOptBench) already move toward functional/operational metrics but are not yet comprehensive

unresolved_questions.statement: How well do LLM-driven generation-and-repair workflows generalize to large-scale, heterogeneous production topologies and multi-vendor environments?
limitations: Existing evidence shows scale-related degradation in benchmarks but relies on synthesized problems or NDT proposals rather than extensive production deployments

unresolved_questions.statement: Which evaluation metrics, validators, and canary/rollback protocols best map to real operational safety (e.g., minimizing unsafe APPLYs, preserving reachability/policy) across NetOps tasks?
limitations: Surveys and individual benchmarks propose metrics but do not converge on a standardized, widely validated operational metric set

unresolved_questions.statement: To what extent can LLM self-correction loops avoid specification-gaming, cognitive-camouflage behaviors, or subtle validator-evasion in complex NetOps tasks?
limitations: Cognitive-camouflage and specification-gaming evidence is cross-domain; dedicated NetOps adversarial studies remain limited

unresolved_questions.statement: How sensitive are NetOps task outcomes to prompt framing, run-to-run stochasticity, and paired vs isolated evaluation designs?
limitations: Studies demonstrate prompt/run sensitivity in related domains; explicit, systematic NetOps prompt-sensitivity experiments are sparse

candidate_gaps.statement: A need remains for standardized, execution-time benchmarks that simulate telemetry faults, stale evidence, and action-constraint checking (i.e., benchmarks that measure unsafe-apply reduction and repair efficacy under telemetry faults).
limitations: WirelessOptBench and Cornetto begin to address this but neither provides a single, broadly adopted standard covering telemetry-fault dynamics across NetOps tasks

candidate_gaps.statement: Insufficient integrated datasets/pipelines that pair LLM prompt–response artifacts with formal verification traces (e.g., Batfish/HSA results) and failure-mode labels to support reproducible training/evaluation of verifier-guided LLM workflows.
limitations: Surveys and prototype papers propose combinations, but publicly available, standardized corpora coupling LLM artifacts with verification traces are limited

candidate_gaps.statement: A formal construct-validity framework tailored to NetOps benchmarks is needed to ensure evaluation evidence maps to operational claims (distinguish ecological/construct/external validity).
limitations: EVE-CV articulates general construct-validity criteria, but domain-specific operational instantiation for NetOps is not yet standardized

candidate_gaps.statement: Limited published work systematically testing adversarial robustness of LLM-generated network configurations (targeted perturbations, prompt-injection, or crafted corner cases that induce unsafe changes).
limitations: There is broad adversarial LLM literature, but explicit adversarial NetOps config-generation studies remain nascent

excluded_claims: LLMs are production-ready for fully autonomous NetOps without deterministic validators, sandbox checks, or rollback/canary controls.
LLM-generated repairs rarely introduce regressions or new faults at scale.
Existing benchmarks already provide fully construct-valid evidence tying LLM outputs to real production operational safety across vendors and topologies.
This record set supports claims about specific single-model superiority across all NetOps tasks (no evidence of blanket model-wide dominance).
